title_en: Contract poker with Jennings and Collins
teaser_en: Jauan Jennings wants a new contract or a trade. Why a new deal is unavoidable and where things stand with Collins.
body_en:
## Why a new contract for Jauan Jennings is unavoidable

With yesterday's report that 49ers wide receiver Jauan Jennings wants either a new contract or a trade, the calm waters right before the start of San Francisco 49ers training camp have turned into at least a few smaller waves.

Jennings is coming off a very good season with 975 yards (only an ejection kept him from 1,000 yards), 77 receptions and 6 touchdowns. After Brandon Aiyuk's injury and Deebo Samuel's slump, he took on responsibility and was one of the few bright spots of last season. On top of that, he was the designated Super Bowl MVP in February 2024 and has generally always been very reliable in the postseason.

He also brings everything it takes to deliver in the Shanahan offense: he is a good and tough route runner, regularly wins contested catches, blocks his opponents all the way into the players' tunnel and knows our scheme inside out. All of these are attributes that have made him so important, especially on key downs, and still do.

He is now entering the last of his two contract years and would earn around $7.5 million in 2025. Assuming that Brandon Aiyuk will still be missing at the start of the season, Deebo Samuel is no longer on the team and our new WR Demarcus Robinson will probably receive a suspension of at least three games, losing another wide receiver would be a severe setback for the Shanahan offense in the coming season.

So he has every reason and very good arguments for a better deal. The 49ers should rather invest in him than in yet another outside wide receiver.

## Defensive tackle Alfred Collins' rookie deal is not signed yet either

The San Francisco 49ers have one more open issue: DT Alfred Collins, like 29 other second-round picks from the 2025 NFL Draft, has not signed a contract yet.

After WR Jayden Higgins (pick 34) signed the first fully guaranteed rookie deal ever for a second-round pick in the NFL with the Houston Texans on May 8, 2025, LB Carson Schwesinger (pick 33) followed suit one day later with the Cleveland Browns, also with a fully guaranteed contract. That means the top two picks of the second round received such deals.

As a result, all second-round picks are now pushing their teams for fully guaranteed contracts. For comparison: across all other draft rounds there are currently exactly three players who have not signed yet, among them first-round pick DB Jahdae Barron.

It is not the first time second-round picks have voiced this demand. But now the 49ers and Collins have to reach an agreement as well, because our rookies are due to report to training camp today.
